name: Central Limit Theorem
miniText: Why can repeated sample means look more regular than the population they summarize? NetLogo Central Limit Theorem builds a bounded population, repeatedly selects groups, and records their sums and means. Lindeberg [1] supplies an original limit-theorem contribution, Durrett [2] presents the probability framework and assumptions, and Berry [3] addresses finite-sample approximation error. Changing the population shape and sample size makes the distinction between individual values and distributions of averages visible. The simulation uses a finite population and an explicit selection procedure; replacement rules and dependence must be considered before applying an independent-sample theorem literally. A larger sample does not make the original population normal. The experiment illustrates convergence ideas and sampling variability under controlled assumptions, while finite histograms alone cannot prove a limiting theorem or establish its applicability to arbitrary real datasets.
